interpretation: The offline replay found lyric candidates for 99/100 songs. In addition, 15 public source pages were manually compared; all 15 normalized full-text hashes differed. These are source-reference observations, but they are not yet adjudicated exact-recording gold. A mismatch does not by itself identify which text is wrong: composition lyrics, aggregator transcripts, and the corpus performance may differ in edition, repeats, or formatting. The former 0/100 was caused by the strict exact-gold gate and did not mean 100 songs were searched and rejected.

referenceEvaluation.interpretation: These 15 source pages are observed comparison references and count toward source-reference coverage. They do not establish exact recording-level ground truth. A full-text mismatch is an observed disagreement, not proof that the selected text is wrong. Classify the diff and edition scope before promoting a correctness claim.

sourceContributions.method: Each discovered source is joined to combineSources output through a SHA-256 source identity. The report marks selected base lyrics, chord contributors, section contributors, and metadata fields separately; it stores no source lyric text or raw candidate IDs.
sourceContributions.interpretation: Candidate availability is now distinct from actual use in the combined document. Counts are songs, not source rows. Contribution is not a correctness claim; separate reference evidence still determines accuracy.

next: Count a traceable source page with checked song/artist match as source-reference coverage. Track exact recording-level gold separately. For each source, record provider attribution when available, URL, title/artist match, edition binding, normalized hash, and a compact diff classification. Promote correctness only after the text is adjudicated for the intended scope.

lyrics.interpretation: Exact normalized lyric or chord-sequence hash agreement, including a shared hash within a conflicting group, is a consolidation signal, not proof of independent provenance or correctness.

chords.interpretation: Exact normalized lyric or chord-sequence hash agreement, including a shared hash within a conflicting group, is a consolidation signal, not proof of independent provenance or correctness.

crossProviderCandidateIdReuse.interpretation: Candidate-ID reuse across provider adapters is not enough to merge or count evidence as independent; compare field payload hashes and provider provenance.
crossProviderCandidateIdReuse.betterLyricsAdapterNote: BetterLyrics uses LRCLIB as its catalog and then resolves lyric content through the Better Lyrics API; a shared catalog ID does not guarantee identical lyric payloads.
